summary: Browser-only redirect script distributed via npm/jsDelivr; no installer-side impact
details: The package ships a browser-only script (px.js) that uses document.write / document.createElement to load an iframe redirecting visitors to https://mfmz.syndagroup.cn/H.html?c=0gjr. package.json declares no preinstall/install/postinstall/prepare lifecycle hooks and the main entry references browser DOM globals (document), so installing or requiring the package under Node.js produces no side effects and no code executes against the installer. A shipped update_px8my.sh reveals a workflow of rotating the redirect destination, bumping the version, republishing to npm, and purging jsDelivr caches — consistent with using npm+jsDelivr as free CDN infrastructure for a redirect gadget. The party at risk is a browser end-user of a site that embeds this script via jsDelivr, not a developer or build system that installs the npm package. Under this engine's installer-centric threat model (exfiltration, RCE, credential theft, backdoor, or install-time destruction against the installer), no attacker-benefit mechanism is present.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
